metadata.note: The Bar Harbor Express and its predecessor the Mount Desert Limited: a seasonal (summer-only) named train connecting Boston to Maine's Mount Desert Island resorts, the classic route for well-off travelers heading to Bar Harbor. Jointly operated by the New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad (from New York, not modeled here -- see below), the Boston and Maine Railroad, and the Maine Central Railroad. Rail reached Mount Desert Ferry (a landing at Hancock Point, where passengers boarded a steamer across Frenchman Bay to Bar Harbor) in 1884-85; the train was renamed the Bar Harbor Express in 1902; the ferry connection was dropped in the mid-1930s in favor of a bus/highway link from Ellsworth as automobile access to the island grew; the route was truncated again to just Boston-Bangor in 1957; and the train was discontinued entirely on Labor Day 1960. Both the Bar Harbor Express and the Maine Central's own Bangor lines used Bangor Union Station (built 1907, demolished 1961 -- the same year Bangor's other historic passenger line, the Bangor and Aroostook, also ended rail passenger service; see bangor_aroostook_railroad.geojson). This file models only the Boston-Bangor-Ellsworth-Hancock Point segment; the historic through cars from New York via the New Haven Railroad along the Northeast Corridor shoreline are not modeled here, since that trackage/era is a separate research question from Maine's own rail history. The Boston-Brunswick portion of the geometry is reused directly from amtrak.geojson's 'Downeaster' shape (same physical Boston & Maine/Maine Central right-of-way still in use today); the Brunswick-Augusta-Waterville-Bangor-Ellsworth-Hancock Point extension is a real-town waypoint approximation, straight-line segments between documented stations, NOT digitized from period track maps.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_Harbor_Express (New York/Boston-Hancock Point train, joint NYNH&H/B&M/MEC operation; began 1902 as a renaming of the earlier Mount Desert Limited; served Mount Desert Ferry 1885-mid-1930s, then Ellsworth and Bangor until 1960; last run Labor Day 1960)
https://www.american-rails.com/bar.html (predecessor Mount Desert Limited; MEC truncated the run to Bangor in 1957, ended the train Labor Day 1960)
data/amtrak.geojson 'Downeaster' feature (GTFS-derived Boston-Brunswick shape, reused here since the Boston & Maine/Maine Central right-of-way is essentially unchanged)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact year within 'mid-1930s' that the Mount Desert Ferry connection was dropped (approximated here as 1935); precise pre-1902 schedule/frequency for the Mount Desert Limited; exact station-by-station routing Brunswick-Bangor-Ellsworth-Hancock Point beyond the well-documented endpoint towns; whether the New York-Boston through cars ran on every trip or only some.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
